content.comment_body: Hi, I tried connecting a [product_name] controller with an expansion module [product_name]. I supplied 220V AC to the controller and tested a simple program. Next, I attached the expansion module to the controller, loaded a new program, and powered everything on. Unfortunately, the expansion module was damaged at the interface side, not the power side, while the controller itself remains operational. I have another module but am hesitant to connect it. I suspect my mistake was not checking AC polarity. Thank you for your support. Cheers, [user_name]
Hi, it's important to supply power simultaneously to both the controller and expansion module.

So, if power wasn't supplied at the same time—maybe that's what happened—could that be why my expansion module failed? To clarify, if I connect power to the controller as L->L and N->N, but accidentally reverse it on the module as L->N and N->L, could that cause the module to burn out on the interface side rather than the power side, even with AC power?
Hello, The 230V is present on the bus connector as well, so if you use two different phases or reverse L and N, it can cause damage or unexpected effects. Regards,

Hi, Powering expansion modules after the base module should not normally result in damage. I think there may be an issue with your wiring. For example, if you use a 230V base module with an analog module that requires 24V, both may not complete their startup simultaneously. In these cases, it's crucial to ensure the base module has time to detect the analog module. Typically, this isn't a problem unless there's a delay with the 24V supply. You can configure the base module startup time from 1 to 10 seconds as needed. Refer to the manual for details. Hope this is helpful.

analysis.insight_summary: Users discussed that incorrect wiring, particularly mismatched AC polarity between the controller and expansion module, led to irreversible damage to the module’s interface while the main controller remained functional. There is a need for guidance regarding proper power wiring and startup timing when using various modules together.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the expansion module to operate reliably when connected to the controller and powered with 230V AC. They also seek clear instructions to avoid hardware failures during wiring and power-up procedures.
